I'll start by reviewing the current repository state.## Where things stand

I reconstructed the full tree from `dump.txt` (334 files, 333 SHA-verified byte-for-byte; `export.sh` is approximate only because the dump embeds its own separator lines) and read the three terminal logs alongside it.

**Slice 32 landed clean.** Your workstation run reports **1074 tests, 0 failed** — exactly the arithmetic prediction — and `ci_local.sh --with-all --with-e2e` passed all eight gates with 16 of 16 §16.3 scenarios green. The handheld reachability barrier passed on its first real run, which is the thing Slice 32 explicitly could not verify from the sandbox. The stress test is worth recording too: 200,000 requests through the quick tunnel, 199,999 × 200 and one 429 (Cloudflare's edge, not the app), p99 ~0.21s.

## What I found while scoping the next slice

**A real finding, and it blocks the work I was about to do.** §11.12 says the stylesheet is written handheld-first through *exactly one* breakpoint. `HandheldLayoutContractTests.TheStylesheetIsWrittenHandheldFirstThroughExactlyOneBreakpoint` reads **only `app.css`**. Every page's inline `<style>` block is invisible to it — so a component can declare its own `@media (max-width: …)` and no gate in the tree notices. Today no component does, so the rule is true; it is just not *enforced*. This is F-46's shape again: a rule stated as a rule and checked against one example.

It stops being hypothetical the moment Stage 1b starts. `HiddenRecords.razor` has `.hidden-record-money { text-align: right }` and a `.hidden-facts` auto-fit grid — both want a narrow/wide difference, and the obvious way to write that is an inline media query on the page. I'd rather fix the gate than write around it silently.

## Proposed Slice 33 — Stage 1b, part one

The two filtered explorers, `EventExplorer.razor` and `HiddenRecords.razor`, plus F-63:

- They are the **last two copies** of the hand-rolled five-link `.admin-header-actions` row that `AdministrationAreaLinks` was built to replace. Each omits itself, so the strip is still a different strip on two of six pages — the exact thing §11.12's "third pill has to be the third pill everywhere" sentence forbids.
- They are also **two copies of one filter form** (`.event-filter` and `.hidden-filter` are the same twelve lines). That becomes a shared `.filter-form` / `.filter-actions` vocabulary in `app.css`, inside the existing single breakpoint.
- Both are already in the area-link list, so both go into `HandheldAdministrationPaths` — the E2E barrier grows from four surfaces to six. `ReachSelector` extends to cover `.filter-actions` controls, which raises the expected count from 7 to 9 (floor 8).
- **F-63:** the breakpoint assertion extends to scan every component `<style>` block, and §11.12's sentence is amended to say "the tree" rather than "the stylesheet".

That leaves `ManageSitting.razor` (1123 lines) and `TableDisplays.razor` (441) for Slice 34, then the `.chip` / `.visually-hidden` de-duplication and the `SharedSelectorPrefixes` extension that empties them.

**Before I build it, one thing worth your veto:** I'm proposing to add both pages to the E2E barrier even though `/administration/hidden-records` will be measured **empty** — populating it needs a guest, a join, an order and a hide, which is scenario 3's and 9's machinery. That's the same trade sittings already makes, and I'd state it in the scenario rather than gloss it. If you'd rather the barrier only visited surfaces with rows on them, say so and I'll leave hidden-records out of the path list and note why.

Say "go" and I'll build it as a structured `.tar.gz` — full files, no diffs, no bespoke text-manipulation scripts, with all documentation (spec §11.12/§16.4 + changelog, `DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md` F-63, `BUILD_PROGRESS.md`, `MENU_AND_HANDHELD_PLAN.md`, `README.md`) landing in the same archive, and an explicit list of files to delete (I expect none).

## Verified before starting

Tree reconstructed from `dump.txt`: 334 files, 333 SHA-256-verified byte-for-byte. Slice 32 is confirmed green on your side — 1074 tests, 0 failed, all eight gates, 16/16 E2E scenarios.

## Two findings, both real

**F-63 — the breakpoint rule is asserted about one file, not the tree.** §11.12 requires exactly one width media query. `HandheldLayoutContractTests.TheStylesheetIsWrittenHandheldFirstThroughExactlyOneBreakpoint` reads only `app.css`; a component's inline `<style>` could declare a second breakpoint and no gate would see it. No component does today, so the rule is true but unenforced — F-46's shape again.

**F-64 — five custom properties are read 55 times and declared nowhere.** This is the one I did not expect. `--muted-foreground` (30 refs), `--rule` (16), `--surface-sunken` (3), `--chip-background` (3), `--chip-foreground` (3), across eight components: `EventExplorer`, `HiddenRecords`, `ManageMenuItem`, `ManagePerson`, `ManageSitting`, `ManageTable`, `TableJoinCode`, `CounterJoinCode`. Every reference falls through to a hard-coded literal, so those eight pages render `#666` greys and `#e5e5e5` hairlines while the rest of the application renders `--ink-soft` `#55636f` and `--hairline` `#e2e6ec`. `var(--undeclared, #666)` is valid CSS with no warning anywhere — which is precisely why nothing noticed. I found it because I was checking EventExplorer's greys, not because I was looking.

## Work completed in the sandbox

- `app.css`: shared `.filter-form` / `.filter-fieldset` / `.filter-choice` / `.filter-choices` / `.filter-actions` / `.filter-count` vocabulary added handheld-first, widened inside the existing single query; `--chip-surface` declared; header comment records the F-63 rule.
- All 55 undeclared-property references rewritten to the properties they should always have named. **Diff-verified: 110 changed lines, every one a `var(--…)` line, no markup touched** — so this cannot break a Razor compile.
- `EventExplorer.razor`: `.page-head` + `AdministrationAreaLinks`, shared filter, inline `.admin-header*` / `.event-filter*` deleted, `margin-left: auto` removed from `.event-when` (it was pushing the timestamp onto its own line on a handset — the wide layout as default).
- `HiddenRecords.razor`: head and filter converted; inline stylesheet edit is where I ran out of calls.
- `HiddenRecordJourneys.cs`: **caught a red-suite trap** — scenario 11's harness pins `form.hidden-filter`, `.hidden-filter-actions`, `p.hidden-count`. Renaming those classes without this file would have failed scenario 11. Selectors repointed; `p.hidden-none` deliberately kept as the harness's handle.

## One scope decision I made without asking

`HandheldLayoutContractTests` grows from four facts to **six**, not five: fact 1 renamed and widened to scan every component `<style>` (F-63); a new fact asserting no component links to two or more of §11.4's six area paths *other than its own route* (which makes "rendered once, not copy-pasted" executable — currently only a doc comment); and a new fact asserting every `var(--name)` in the tree is declared in `:root` (F-64). Predicted count **1076**, arithmetic from your observed 1074, not an observation.

I took F-64's fix into this slice rather than deferring it behind a second migration list, on F-47's reasoning: a list that exists to defer a name substitution is a list that shouldn't exist. If you'd rather I hadn't touched `ManageSitting` and `ManagePerson` a slice early, say so.

I verified the archive extracts to exactly those 19 paths, is byte-identical to what I built, and that applying it over a pristine copy of your tree leaves all six contract facts passing.

The work
EventExplorer.razor and HiddenRecords.razor join §11.12's shared vocabulary. They were the last two pages carrying a hand-rolled copy of §11.4's area-link row — five <a class="button-secondary"> in a .admin-header-actions div, each copy omitting its own page — and the only two carrying a filter form. §16.3 scenario 16 goes from four surfaces to six.

Two findings, neither in the work I set out to do
F-63 — §11.12's exactly one breakpoint is a rule about the tree, asserted about app.css alone, while the same section grants twenty-one components an inline <style>. No component had a second breakpoint, so the rule was true and unenforced — the same kind of true F-59 was. Found by needing to write one.

F-64 — five custom properties read 55 times across eight components, declared nowhere. var(--muted-foreground, #666) is valid CSS with no warning from anything in this stack, so eight surfaces drew #666 greys and 
#e5e5e5 hairlines while the rest of the application drew --ink-soft and --hairline. The mechanism is a fallback — which is what a careful author writes — so the wrong code reads as more careful than the correct code would.

Three decisions to veto if you want to
F-64 fixed across all eight files, not just the two I was rewriting. The alternative was a deferral list; F-47 says don't write a list whose only job is to defer a name substitution. Applied programmatically, diff-verified at 110 changed lines, every one a var(--…) line. Cost: ManageSitting and ManagePerson get touched twice.
/administration/hidden-records measured empty — same terms sittings already was. Its filter submit is measured, so it isn't contributing nothing.
Eight pages will look slightly different. That's the palette they were always meant to draw, but it's visible and it's a judgement, so it's yours.
Run
bash scripts/check_tree.sh
bash scripts/ci_local.sh --with-all --with-e2e
Expect 8 gates, 1076 tests / 0 failed (was 1074 — two new [Fact]; arithmetic, not an observation), 16 of 16 scenarios with scenario 16 walking six surfaces and measuring nine controls. The gate-1 file count doesn't move.

Worth knowing before you run it
I caught a red suite that would otherwise have shipped: HiddenRecordJourneys.cs pins form.hidden-filter, .hidden-filter-actions and p.hidden-count. Renaming those without that file fails scenario 11 on a page that is correct. Repointed; p.hidden-none deliberately kept, because it's the harness's handle rather than a style.

Nothing compiled and no browser rendered anything. Every fact was ported to Python and executed (six pass here, five fail against your current tree), eight planted regressions were all caught, and balance/CS1620/CS4007/tag-tree/hygiene are clean with untouched siblings as controls — but the Razor files are still the likely site of a compiler complaint, and the CSS claims rest on reading app.css rather than on a measurement.

docs/DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md closes with a note I'd rather you disagreed with than skipped: F-58, F-62, F-63 and F-64 were all found by adjacency — being near something for an unrelated reason — not by any of this project's sweeps. That doesn't scale and can't be scheduled, and the only cheap consequence I could find is the one this slice acted on.
